title: Iran’s Prince of Persia APT Hosts C&C in US for First Time Since 2016
description: The Iranian state-sponsored APT group known as Prince of Persia resumed operations in 2026 after a three-month pause coinciding with the Iran-US-Israel conflict. The group deployed a new Tornado malware command-and-control (C&C) server hosted in the United States for the first time since 2016, using shared hosting services rather than virtual private servers. Prince of Persia targets Iranian dissidents and government and private entities in the US, Europe, and the Middle East. The group uses malware capable of stealing files via Telegram bots. Semperis researchers have shared indicators of compromise and recommend monitoring for related activity.
aiSummary: Prince of Persia, an Iranian government-sponsored advanced persistent threat (APT) group active for nearly 20 years, paused operations for three months in early 2026 during the Iran-US-Israel conflict. After this lull, the group resumed data theft operations using its Tornado malware family. Notably, it hosted a Tornado second-stage command-and-control server on US shared hosting infrastructure in 2026, the first US-based C&C server since 2016. This server was hosted on Namecheap shared hosting, a departure from prior use of virtual private servers. The group also deployed additional infrastructure behind Cloudflare. Tornado malware capabilities include file theft via Telegram bots. Semperis has tracked the group’s infrastructure and shared IoCs for defensive use.
aiImpact: Prince of Persia’s operations involve targeted espionage and data theft, primarily against Iranian dissidents and entities in the US, Europe, and the Middle East. The deployment of a US-hosted C&C server may complicate attribution and takedown efforts. The group’s malware has successfully exfiltrated thousands of files from victims. The impact is primarily espionage and data compromise, with no evidence of broader disruption or destructive activity reported.
